label: Motorcycle
title: Motorcycle safety
headline: Your gear is your bodywork
intro: On a motorbike there's no cabin, no airbag and no seatbelt. What you wear is all that stands between you and the road.

contentNotice.text: Some parts talk about head injuries and the risk of being killed. Injuries are shown as simple diagrams, never as people.

topics.title: Helmets
topics.blurb: What a helmet does in a fall

scenes.question: Wearing a helmet correctly cuts a motorcyclist's risk of brain injury by up to how much?

lines: You've got a lift home from a friend on a motorbike. It's only a few streets.
There's one helmet, and your friend is wearing it.

art.alt: A rider pictogram in everyday clothes, with no helmet.

scenes.prompt: Compare the impact on a test head form with and without a helmet.

art.alt: A plain head form dropped onto a test block. Colours show where the impact would cause injury.

states.label: No helmet
states.caption: Without a helmet, the full force goes straight into the skull and brain.

states.label: Helmet
states.caption: The helmet's shell spreads the blow and its foam lining crushes slowly, so far less force reaches the brain.

scenes.explain: Wearing a helmet correctly cuts the risk of brain injury by up to {claim:int.who.helmet-brain}. A rider without one is more than {claim:int.who.helmet-death} as likely to die in a crash.

questions.prompt: Only the rider has to wear a helmet. A passenger can ride without one.
questions.reason: Both the rider and the passenger must wear a motorcycle helmet that fits, with the chin strap done up. The rider must make sure any passenger younger than {claim:na.law.helmet-child} wears one properly.

questions.prompt: How many people may ride on a motorbike without a side-car?

options.label: As many as fit on the seat

questions.reason: No more than {claim:na.law.moto-pillion} people may ride a motorbike: the rider and one passenger.

questions.prompt: When must a motorbike's headlight be on?
questions.reason: A motorbike's headlight must be on at all times, so other drivers see you sooner.

lines: Every ride, every rider: helmet on and strapped, even for a short trip.
If there's only one helmet, the second person doesn't ride.
A cracked or dropped helmet won't protect you again. Replace it.

scenes.question: Compared with a rider wearing a helmet correctly, how many times as likely is a rider without one to die in a crash?

lines: It's hot, and you're only riding to the shops. Shorts and slops feel fine.
Then a car pulls out without seeing you, and you go down.

art.alt: A rider pictogram in shorts, a T-shirt and slops.

scenes.prompt: In a slide, the road acts like sandpaper. Compare everyday clothes with full riding gear.

art.alt: A rider pictogram, front view, with the body areas that gear protects marked.

states.label: Everyday clothes
states.caption: Shorts, a T-shirt and slops wear through in moments. Hands, knees and feet take the worst of it.

states.label: Full gear
states.caption: A jacket, gloves, long trousers and boots made for riding take the scraping instead of your skin.

art.alt: The rider pictogram in full gear, with one body area highlighted at a time.

steps.title: Helmet
steps.body: Protects your brain. Choose one that fits snugly and fasten the strap every time.

steps.title: Jacket
steps.body: Tough material with armour at the shoulders, elbows and back.

steps.title: Gloves
steps.body: Your hands go down first in a fall. Gloves keep your palms and fingers working.

steps.title: Trousers
steps.body: Long, tough trousers protect your hips and knees, not shorts.

steps.title: Boots
steps.body: Cover your ankles. Slops come off and leave your feet bare.

steps.title: Be seen
steps.body: Bright or reflective colours help drivers spot you, day and night.

scenes.explain: A rider without a helmet is more than {claim:int.who.helmet-death} as likely to die in a crash. The rest of your gear decides how badly you're hurt.

lines: Dress for the slide, not the ride: jacket, gloves, long trousers, boots.
Bright colours and your headlight help drivers see you.
Ride as if nobody has seen you, because often they haven't.

scenes.title: The quick trip
scenes.label: A made-up story, based on common situations
scenes.warning: This story mentions a rider being hurt. It doesn't describe the injury in detail.
paragraphs: Tomas only borrowed his cousin's bike to fetch bread. It was five minutes away, so he left the helmet on the hook and rode in a T-shirt.
A taxi stopped suddenly in front of him. He braked, slid, and went down on the tar.
His arms and knees were badly scraped and his wrist was broken. 'The doctor said my head missed the kerb by a hand's width,' he says.
Now the helmet and gloves go on before the engine starts, however short the trip.

signpost.text: If a crash has affected you or someone close to you, you don't have to deal with it alone. LifeLine/ChildLine Namibia offers free counselling: call {claim:na.support.lifeline}.
